claims.claim: Tesseract.js wraps browser/server OCR, and does not directly support PDFs.
claims.finding: Opened official repository and Project Scope section. It describes WebAssembly wrapping of Tesseract for browser/Node use and no PDF support. The current site's tool is further restricted to one still PNG/JPEG/WebP; no general handwriting or layout accuracy promise is made.

claims.claim: Sufficient resolution matters, and upscaling can improve some recognition results.
claims.finding: Opened API recognition guidance, including its sufficiently high-resolution input note. It supports trying a larger input; article explains that resizing cannot restore missing detail and does not guarantee improvement.

claims.claim: Tesseract image preparation guidance covers rotation, reasonable borders, noise, uneven backgrounds, and scan resolution.
claims.finding: Opened the quality guide's rescaling, binarisation, noise, rotation and border sections. It recommends horizontal lines, reasonable borders and at least 300 dpi scan input. Article scopes DPI as documentation guidance, not a browser admission/accuracy threshold. It gives no measured accuracy or glare/Spanish benchmark.

claims.claim: Tesseract.js can use explicit worker, core, and language-file paths rather than default external support-file downloads.
claims.finding: Opened local installation guide and compared with current AiBrowserTool.tsx/browserOcrWorker.ts. These set self-hosted same-origin worker/core/language paths. Documentation examples contain older versions; actual app versions and native-worker behavior are evidenced separately below. Local paths do not establish page-wide offline behavior or anonymity.
